# SEO-498: Declare the feed with an alternate link and its media type

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `feeds` |
| Category | `SEARCH_DISCOVERABILITY` |
| Minimum level | `RECOMMENDED` |
| Severity | `MEDIUM` |
| Impact | `LOW` |
| Change safety | `SAFE_AUTOMATIC` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Pages the feed covers carry a link element pointing at the feed, giving the feed's media type and an absolute address, so a reader can find the feed from any page in the section.

## Rationale

Without that link a reader has to guess the feed's path, and a link that omits the media type gives no way to tell a feed from any other alternate representation.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_feeds"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Emit the link from the same configuration that generates the feed, so the declared address and the served address cannot diverge. Point section pages at their own section feed rather than at the site feed.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Collect alternate feed links per route, fetch each declared address, and confirm the media type served matches the type the link declares.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `HTTP_HEADER`, `FEED`
- Automated check: `feed-alternate-link-declared`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_NEWS`, `SOCIAL_PREVIEW`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: Adding a link to a feed that already exists changes no behaviour and is reversible, which is why it is permitted automatically. Creating a feed is not covered by this record.
